decks.notes: The main concept of this deck is to disrupt the opponent's game plan by utilizing artifacts that restrict their resources and enable aggressive creatures to quickly finish the game. By utilizing cards like Sphere of Resistance, Chalice of the Void, and Null Rod to slow down the opponent, along with powerful artifact creatures like Patchwork Automaton and Stonecoil Serpent, this deck aims to overwhelm the opponent before they can establish their own strategy. The deck also includes mana acceleration from Mishra's Workshop and powerful artifact tutors like Karn, the Great Creator to ensure a consistent and powerful board presence.

This deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan with a combination of counterspells, removal, and disruptive creatures like Lavinia, Azorius Renegade. It also has powerful card advantage and selection tools like Force of Will, Ancestral Recall, and Dig Through Time. The inclusion of cards like Orcish Bowmasters and Psychic Frog offer additional control elements, while the combo of Dress Down and Lórien Revealed can shut down opposing threats. With efficient mana sources like Moxen and fetch lands, the deck aims to outlast the opponent and grind out a victory through attrition and resource denial.

The deck focuses on using the powerful mana acceleration provided by Mishra's Workshop and mana artifacts to quickly deploy disruptive threats like Null Rod, Sphere of Resistance, and Lodestone Golem. The goal is to slow down the opponent's game plan while maintaining pressure with efficient creatures like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Scrawling Crawler. Additionally, the deck is able to generate card advantage and resilience through Crucible of Worlds and Inventors' Fair, ensuring that it can outlast the opponent in a resource war.

This deck focuses on using Paradoxical Outcome to generate massive card advantage and mana while setting up combos to win the game quickly. The deck includes fast mana sources like Moxen and Black Lotus, along with powerful blue spells like Ancestral Recall and Force of Will to control the game. The presence of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value to be gained by recurring cheap artifacts. Overall, the deck aims to assemble key pieces efficiently and overwhelm the opponent with a powerful combo finish.

This Dimir Control deck focuses on using efficient removal spells and disruptive counterspells to control the game while also utilizing card advantage through draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time. The deck also includes powerful synergy with cards like Mishra's Bauble and Orcish Bowmasters to gain incremental advantage. Lurrus of the Dream-Den acts as a Companion to provide additional value by recurring key cards from the graveyard. Overall, the deck aims to outlast opponents and establish dominance through careful resource management and strategic plays.

The main idea of this Dimir Control deck is to disrupt and control the opponent's game plan while generating card advantage through spells like Ancestral Recall, Dig Through Time, and Treasure Cruise. With a focus on countering spells with Force of Will and Force of Negation, along with removing threats with Fatal Push and Wasteland, this deck aims to out-value and out-control its opponent. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value in the late game by allowing for recurring spells and permanents.

The deck focuses on using hatebears to disrupt the opponent's strategy while applying pressure through aggressive creatures. It utilizes powerful artifacts like Sol Ring and Moxen for fast mana acceleration, along with disruptive cards like Null Rod to shut down opposing artifact strategies. The deck aims to control the game with cards like Archon of Emeria and Clarion Conqueror to slow down the opponent, while deploying efficient creatures like Seasoned Dungeoneer and White Plume Adventurer to chip away at the opponent's life total. The deck also includes removal spells like Swords to Plowshares and Wasteland to deal with opposing threats.

The deck focuses on using Paradoxical Outcome to generate card advantage and mana acceleration, allowing the player to set up powerful combos involving artifacts like Time Vault and Bolas's Citadel. It also includes disruption cards like Force of Will and Mental Misstep to protect the combo pieces and disrupt the opponent's game plan. The deck has a strong tutoring package with cards like Demonic Tutor and Vampiric Tutor, as well as utility lands like Tolarian Academy to further enhance the deck's synergy and power.

The deck focuses on efficiently assembling the combo pieces needed to win the game using the Doomsday card. It includes various powerful cards like Ancestral Recall, Black Lotus, Demonic Tutor, and Force of Will to enable the combo and protect it from disruption. The deck also includes card draw and selection spells like Brainstorm, Preordain, and Gitaxian Probe to set up the Doomsday pile effectively. With careful planning and precise execution, the deck aims to win the game in a single turn after resolving Doomsday.

The deck aims to disrupt and control the opponent's resources while generating card advantage through powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall, Dig Through Time, and Treasure Cruise. It also utilizes powerful disruption spells like Force of Will, Force of Negation, and Null Rod to disrupt the opponent's game plan. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for continuous access to key pieces of the deck from the sideboard. Overall, the deck focuses on controlling the game, disrupting opponents, and generating card advantage to secure victory.

The primary focus of this Dimir Control deck is to disrupt the opponent's strategy through a combination of counter spells, removal, and disruptive permanents while generating card advantage through card draw and recursion. The deck aims to control the game by efficiently dealing with threats and maintaining card advantage to outvalue the opponent. By utilizing powerful cards like Force of Will, Ancestral Recall, and Demonic Tutor, the deck aims to control the tempo of the game and eventually win through incremental advantage and efficient use of resources.

This deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan while applying pressure with efficient creatures. By playing hatebears like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex, the deck aims to slow down the opponent's spells and mana development. The inclusion of Anointed Peacekeeper and Seasoned Dungeoneer provides additional disruption and card advantage, while cards like Clarion Conqueror and White Plume Adventurer give the deck a strong aggressive element. With a few powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen for fast mana acceleration, this deck aims to control the game and win through aggressive plays.

The main concept of this Dredge combo deck is to quickly fill the graveyard with cards and utilize cards like Narcomoeba, Creeping Chill, and Prized Amalgam to bring back powerful creatures for aggressive plays. The deck also includes disruption cards like Force of Will and Force of Negation to protect the combo pieces. Bazaar of Baghdad is essential for filling the graveyard efficiently, while Golgari Thug, Golgari Grave-Troll, and Stinkweed Imp help with dredging cards. Overall, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with fast graveyard recursion and combo potential.

This deck focuses on quickly assembling the necessary resources to cast Paradoxical Outcome and generate a large amount of card advantage and mana through the bouncing of artifacts. It aims to combo off by chaining multiple spells together, using mana rocks like Moxen and Mana Crypt to generate the necessary mana to draw through the deck and find win conditions. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value and recursion, while cards like Force of Will and Flusterstorm help protect the combo and disrupt the opponent's game plan.

This deck focuses on quickly filling up the graveyard with creatures and using Bazaar of Baghdad to dig for key cards. By utilizing cards like Blazing Rootwalla and Hollow One in combination with cards like Vengevine and Fury, the deck aims to put early pressure on the opponent and close out the game quickly. The deck also includes disruptive elements like Force of Will and Wasteland to control the game. Overall, the strategy revolves around leveraging the graveyard as a resource and overwhelming the opponent with aggressive creatures.

This deck focuses on generating a large amount of mana quickly through cards like Dark Ritual and Sol Ring, and then using that mana to cast powerful spells like Bolas's Citadel and Tendrils of Agony in order to win the game in a single turn. It includes cards that provide card advantage and ways to protect the combo, ensuring that the player can assemble their win condition efficiently and effectively. The key strategy is to set up a chain of spells that generate storm count, and then finish the opponent off with a massive Tendrils of Agony.
